task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about how Willowmere Library handles requests to reconsider a book's place in its collection. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Willowmere Library has received two formal reconsideration requests concerning the invented novel The Mirror Road.
The novel is currently cataloged for adults, and the requests concern its display and collection placement rather than a supplied finding of a cataloging error.
A separate petition with 58 signatures accompanies one request; signatures are not counted as 58 completed review applications.
The library's published policy asks a requester to identify the work, describe the concern and state the action sought.
A staff review group reads the work and considers the collection policy, intended audience and the specific concerns in the request.
Under the current local policy, a request does not automatically remove the book from circulation while the review is pending.
The review may recommend retaining the current placement, changing placement or another action supported by the collection policy.
Library manager Orla Senn said, "We need to consider the whole work and the actual request, rather than decide from a sentence on a form."
The current requests raise concerns about readers encountering a distressing bereavement scene without expecting it.
Request organizer Dara Vell said, "We want the library to explain how the display tells readers what sort of book they are choosing."
The packet does not reproduce any passage from the invented novel and makes no claim about a real author or book.
The staff group will issue a written recommendation with reasons, which the requester may ask the library board to review.
Board review is a separate stage, not an automatic citywide vote on the book.
The board has not yet considered these requests or made a final decision about the novel.
The library will publish the final decision and its policy basis without publishing private contact information from the request forms.
The policy covers items already in the collection and is distinct from a request that the library purchase a new title.
Library staff still make ordinary display changes during the year; a moved display is not by itself evidence that a formal challenge succeeded.
The library has one circulating copy and one book-group copy of the novel, but the packet provides no current borrowing total.
The book-group copy was acquired through the library's regular group-reading budget rather than a donation with placement conditions.
Residents can obtain the policy and request form on paper at the desk as well as through the library's website.
The policy sets a response process but does not guarantee every requester the action they prefer.
This packet describes Willowmere's institutional procedure, not a general legal conclusion about book restrictions elsewhere.

forbidden_additions: An already banned book, 58 separate formal requests or a final board decision.
Invented passages, borrowing figures or claims about a real author.
A public vote or universal legal rule substituted for the supplied policy.
preserve: The requesters' stated display concern and the library's whole-work review.
Separate staff and board stages without assuming the outcome.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
